findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can corrupt or leak indexes
findings.body: BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu during index creation and builder execution, and the cache is only populated at line 137 after the build completes. Concurrent callers for the same NamespacedResource (for example searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex, which has no per-key deduplication, racing the parallel startup builds in searchSupport.init) can therefore both pass GetIndex, both create a bleve index, and for file-backed indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory path, causing lock/already-exists failures or corruption; whichever finishes last silently overwrites cache[key] without closing the earlier index, leaking its file handles/memory. The lock needs to remain finer-grained but still deduplicate/serialize builds per key and close any replaced index.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu.RLock. With BuildIndex now inserting into b.cache (lines 137-139) while other builds/searches may be running, and searchSupport.init now calling TotalDocs for its completion log after parallel builds, this concurrent map iteration versus map write can trigger Go's fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' panic and crash the process. TotalDocs should snapshot or iterate the cache under RLock (taking care not to hold it during slow DocCount calls if that reintroduces contention).

findings.title: Failed startup Init leaks the server's background context and watch goroutines
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) before returning, but on error it only logs and returns nil, err without calling s.cancel() or Stop. If initialization partially succeeds -- e.g. search.init succeeds and starts its WatchWriteEvents goroutine/poller in searchSupport.init, then initWatcher fails -- the constructed server is discarded yet its background context (created at line 229) is never cancelled, so the search watcher, backend poller, and any blob/backend resources keep running for a server that failed to start. Cleanup (cancel/Stop) should run on the Init error path.
